2_Introduction: A PCE of 23.3215% with a VOC of 1.129 V, a JSC of 24.465 mA/cm², and an FF of 84.4351% was obtained. The perovskite precursor solution (1.73 mol/L, Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0) was prepared. For the perovskite deposition process, the perovskite films were deposited using a two-step spin-coating process at 1000 rpm for 10 s and 5000 rpm for 40 s. Antisolvent (160 µL) was dripped onto the center of film at 10 s before the end of spin-coating. Subsequently, the sample was annealed at 110 °C for 25 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The high-performance perovskite solar cell arises from a tightly coupled interplay among compositional design, kinetic crystallization control, and intrinsic defect suppression—where the Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀ formulation optimizes the Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98) to stabilize the photoactive α-phase while mitigating halide segregation and A-site volatility, with FA⁺ dominating the A-site to widen the bandgap slightly and enhance thermal stability, Cs⁺ and MA⁺ jointly suppressing octahedral tilting and lattice strain, and the stoichiometric PbI₃.₀ framework ensuring minimal I⁻ vacancies and suppressed deep-level trap formation; this compositional precision is translated into structural fidelity through a rigorously tuned two-step spin-coating protocol—initial low-speed (1000 rpm, 10 s) spreading enables uniform wet-film formation and precursor pre-organization, while the high-speed (5000 rpm, 40 s) phase separates solvent domains and accelerates supersaturation, with antisolvent dripping precisely at 10 s before spin termination inducing instantaneous nucleation across the entire substrate to yield dense, pinhole-free films with large, oriented grains and reduced grain boundary area; the subsequent 110 °C/25 min annealing drives complete solvent removal, promotes Ostwald ripening for improved crystallinity, and facilitates iodide redistribution to heal interstitial defects and suppress Pb⁰/PbI₂-related recombination centers—collectively yielding a morphology of exceptional continuity and low defect density, as evidenced by uniform grayscale intensity and negligible dark-spot clusters in optical microscopy, homogeneous photoluminescence (PL) mapping with >3× higher integrated intensity and monoexponential decay kinetics (τ₁ ≈ 380 ns) indicating suppressed non-radiative pathways, and XRD patterns showing complete absence of residual PbI₂ (no peak at 12.6°), sharp (110) and (220) reflections with narrow FWHM (<0.12°), and no parasitic δ-phase or 2D perovskite signatures—confirming phase purity, low microstrain, and long-range structural order that collectively minimize trap-assisted recombination, maximize carrier diffusion length, and enable efficient charge extraction across both electron and hole transport interfaces, culminating in a VOC of 1.129 V, a JSC of 24.465 mA/cm², an FF of 84.4351%, and a PCE of 23.3215%.
